plan_a_advantages: Includes a tempo run, essential for speed development.
Incorporates aerobic runs to build endurance and speed.
Has a more balanced mix of training intensities.
plan_b_advantages: Higher rest day frequency may be beneficial for recovery, especially for beginners.
The longer long run could build more endurance, though at the expense of speed development.
reasoning: While both plans aim to improve trail running speed, Plan A is the better choice for someone seeking that goal. Plan A incorporates a tempo run, which is crucial for developing the speed and lactate threshold necessary for faster trail running. Plan B focuses almost exclusively on easy running and a single long run, which is more suited for building base endurance rather than speed development. The inclusion of aerobic runs in Plan A, alongside the tempo session, provides a more well-rounded approach to improving trail running performance.
